NO JUDGED AWARD EXISTS for hot chocolate in Britain, so this ranking rests on editorial and independent consensus alone, with nothing judged to anchor it.
Time Out's list is four years old and shares zero names with The Infatuation's. Every Time Out name needs a trading check before it is printed.
Badiani resolves to the Covent Garden branch; sources name Soho. Multi-branch, needs a branch decision before an address is printed.

sources.name: Time Out - The 16 Best Hot Chocolates in London
sources.note: UNORDERED listicle, no ranks carried. DATED 28 OCTOBER 2022 - four years old, and it shares ZERO names with The Infatuation's current guide. Trading status must be checked on every name before any of them reaches an article. Reached via a /blog/ten-indulgent-hot-chocolates URL that redirects here; one page, not two.

quotes.Dark Sugars Cocoa House: The scent of Ghanaian cocoa beans wafts up Brick Lane. Hot chocolate intense, in numerous flavours, covered in real shaved chocolate.
quotes.Chin Chin Dessert Club: A paper cup topped with a giant orb of handmade marshmallow, blowtorched to charred, sticky decadence. Also does a vegan version with raspberry and apricot.
quotes.Rabot 1745: Hotel Chocolat's cafe overlooking Borough Market, named for a cocoa estate founded in 1745 in St Lucia. You can add a shot of St Lucian rum.
quotes.Melange: Peckham, run by chocolatier Isabelle Alaya, OPEN WEEKENDS ONLY as of this list. Salted caramel is the biggest hit; white chocolate with matcha also sold.

sources.name: The Infatuation - The 8 Best Hot Chocolates In London
sources.note: UNORDERED, no ranks. THE FINDING OF THIS PASS: shares not one name with Time Out's 16. Two serious sources, two disjoint lists - the whole-list divergence case in the method, and almost certainly because Time Out's is four years stale.

sources.name: Insider / Food Insider (YouTube)
sources.note: ONE PUBLISHER, TWO CHANNELS, ONE SOURCE. @InsiderFood and @Insider are both Business Insider and are merged here, the same rule that makes a masthead's guide and its YouTube channel one opinion. Four relevant videos, 8.4M views on the largest. Names taken from the descriptions, not the titles.

quotes.Said Dal 1923: A London cafe that sells melted chocolate to drink out of decorative cups. Insider asks whether the Instagram-worthy drink is too gooey and over the top.
quotes.Dark Sugars Cocoa House: 72 kinds of chocolate all made in-house. The base is chocolate paste topped with hot milk, more froth, and three types of chocolate shavings.

sources.name: Rayscafe (YouTube)
sources.note: Lists its four stops in the description under 'Featured hot chocolate spots', which is exactly where the method says to look.

sources.name: thiswasnotwellplanned (YouTube)
sources.note: Description carries full addresses and a per-venue verdict, which is unusually good sourcing for the tier. Description was truncated at capture - RE-READ for the stops after Italian Bear before treating this list as complete.

quotes.William Curley: 33 Smith's Ct, London W1D 7DP. Their review: dark hot chocolate was a bit too sweet and milky for us.

quotes.Italian Bear Chocolate: Poured triple-layered - thick, creamy and smooth.

quotes.Dark Sugars Cocoa House: Films the making of the hot chocolates at the Brick Lane shop.
Filmed at the Shoreditch shop - CHECK WHICH BRANCH, the other sources name Brick Lane.

quotes.Said Dal 1923: Triple chocolate with cinnamon. Located Covent Garden per this source - Time Out's older page calls it Soho. CHECK THE ADDRESS.

sources.name: Mostly Food and Travel - London's dreamiest hot chocolates
sources.note: CARRIES THE ALIAS FINDING OF THIS PASS. Writes 'Italian Bear (previously SAID DAAL)', which if true means Italian Bear Chocolate and Said Dal 1923 are one site under two names - four citations and two citations that may be six for one venue. NOT merged; see openVenueQuestions.

sources.name: DesignMyNight - Where To Find London's Best Hot Chocolate
sources.note: TRAP 8 CHECKED AND PASSED. DesignMyNight contributed pure page furniture on afternoon tea and seafood and was removed from both, so this page was read before recording - it is a real guide with named venues AND published prices, organised as 'The Boozy One', 'The Ube One' and so on. Prices are the most useful thing any source here carries.

quotes.Chin Chin Dessert Club: Hot chocolate £4.95, marshmallow flamed at the counter.
quotes.Knoops: From £4, the customisable one - you pick the cocoa percentage.
quotes.Fire and Fromage: Hot chocolate £5, with an optional £4 shot of Black Cow vodka.
quotes.The Chocolate Cocktail Club: Bottomless chocolate cocktails, £32 per person - a drinking experience rather than a cafe.

sources.name: Clumsy Girl Travels - 16 Amazing Places for Hot Chocolate in London
sources.note: Independent travel blog, unordered. Reaches further than any other source here - Fuwa Fuwa, Leonidas, Adam Handling's chocolate shop and Mercato Mayfair appear nowhere else in this corpus. That breadth is also a reason to check each name individually rather than trusting the list wholesale.

declined.name: Time Out - Hot damn! It's your favourite hot chocolate in London
declined.reason: SAME DOMAIN as the Time Out record above, so it could never be a second opinion. Also a READER POLL from 17 November 2015 rather than an editorial list, and eleven years stale. Its names - Said, Dark Sugars, Paul A Young, Cantina Laredo, Cafe Bonito, Betty Blythe, Caffe Vergnano, The Urban Chocolatier - are deliberately NOT merged: an eleven-year-old reader vote is not evidence of current quality, and merging would inflate counts for venues that may not trade.

declined.name: Joshua Weissman, Tasting History, Dished, Downshiftology, BuzzFeedVideo, Les Frenchies
declined.reason: Returned by the same search but off-topic: recipes, history, instant-cocoa taste tests, and one guide to hot chocolate in PARIS. None names a London venue.

declined.name: Jennifer Earle - The Next Delicious Thing
declined.reason: THE SPECIALIST FOR THIS TOPIC AND STILL NOT USABLE. She runs Chocolate Ecstasy Tours, posts weekly, and is exactly what tier C is for - but the archive carries no hot chocolate list, and the one relevant London chocolate post is PAYWALLED and discloses a hosted visit: 'Their team invited me down to check it out.' That is the venue's own marketing wearing a writer's face, which is what tier F excludes. Re-check if she publishes an unhosted hot chocolate piece.

openVenueQuestions: CHIN CHIN: Time Out writes 'Chin Chin Dessert Club', Insider and Rayscafe write 'Chin Chin Labs'. Recorded here under the Time Out spelling on the assumption they are one business, but this needs confirming and an alias adding - if wrong, it hands a three-source count to a venue that earned less.
DARK SUGARS: named as Brick Lane by Time Out and Halal Gems, Shoreditch by settime2588. Likely two branches of one business - carry as Branches rows, not two venues.
SAID DAL 1923: Covent Garden per Onion Jain, Soho per the 2015 Time Out page. Confirm the address before printing an area.
ITALIAN BEAR CHOCOLATE / 'The Italian Bear': alias needed, 41 Broadwick St W1F 9QL.
KNOOPS is a multi-branch chain (Covent Garden, Kensington, Chelsea, Notting Hill, Richmond at least). Sources name the brand, not a branch. Carry as branches rows.

HOTEL CHOCOLAT vs RABOT 1745 - Rabot 1745 IS Hotel Chocolat's Borough Market cafe. Time Out names Rabot 1745; Clumsy Girl names Hotel Chocolat. Probably one venue, possibly two products. Check before counting.

BADIANI and VENCHI are gelato chains that also pour chocolate; Black Sheep Coffee and ABC Kitchens are not chocolate businesses at all. Decide whether a coffee chain's hot chocolate belongs in this guide before it inherits a citation.

placesRun.scope: 22 rows - the 9 venues on 2+ sources plus the 13 Time Out-only names. 27 calls total including a 5-row re-run to correct bad matches, 0.54% of the free monthly tier.
placesRun.theResult: TIME OUT'S 2022 LIST DOES NOT STAND UP. Of its 13 unique names, 3 are CLOSED_PERMANENTLY and 4 more cannot be resolved to a hot chocolate business at all - 7 of 13 dead or gone in four years. That is why the trading check came before the writing.
closedPermanently: Paul A Young Fine Chocolates (W1F 8WA) - the best-known chocolatier on the list.
couldNotResolve: Rabot 1745 - resolves to 'Rabot 1745 Beauty' in White City (W12 7GF) even with the hood set to Borough Market. Hotel Chocolat's Borough Market cafe appears to be gone and only the beauty line still carries the name.
Intermission - resolves to 'Intermission Film' (N1 6NU), a different business.
Cafe La Divina - resolves to 'La Divina Italian Restaurant' (N1 1QP), probably a different business.
Apres Food Co - resolves to 'Apres Burgers' (SW10 0BH), a different business.
placesRun.note: The four above are NOT recorded as closed - Places matched a different business, which is not the same as proving the original is gone. They are unverified and must not be printed as either open or closed.

resolvedVenueQuestions: ITALIAN BEAR = SAID DAL 1923, RESOLVED 2026-09-07. Places resolves BOTH names to 'Italian Bear Chocolate - Soho' at W1F 9QL. Two independent confirmations: Mostly Food and Travel already wrote 'Italian Bear (previously SAID DAAL)', and the enrichment lands both on one postcode. Italian Bear took over Said's Broadwick Street site. MERGING THEM MAKES IT THE MOST-CITED VENUE IN THE TOPIC on 9, ahead of Dark Sugars on 8.
CHIN CHIN, RESOLVED 2026-09-07. Places returns 'Chin Chin Dessert Club (Chin Chin Ice...)' at W1D 3DS, confirming Dessert Club and Labs are one business. The 6 citations stand.
